title: a deployable named like the context it hosts (`deployable claims` hosting `context Claims`) — on elixir the app module and the context facade share a name (`Claims` / `Claims.Claims`)
note: Minted by the claims developer-persona eval (wave 2).  Every elixir controller opened with `alias Claims.Claims`, which rebinds `Claims` itself, so the same file's `rescue guard_error in Claims.GuardError` resolved to `Claims.Claims.GuardError` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` failed — while `generate system` reported `0 error(s), 0 warning(s)`.  Repaired, not refused: when the context name equals the app module the controller drops the facade alias and calls `Claims.Claims.<fn>` fully qualified (`contextCallRef` in `src/generator/elixir/vanilla/denial.ts`), so every non-clashing model stays byte-identical.  Both controller emitters (relational + event-sourced) are exercised.  The row is ALL because the other four backends have no alias semantics here and must keep compiling the same names.

apiCaller.e2eLess: The defect is an elixir COMPILE failure (`alias Claims.Claims` shadowing the app module in every controller, so `Claims.GuardError` was undefined); the fix only changes how the controller spells the facade, which is not observable on the wire.  `corpus-elixir-build` is its oracle.  Signed with its reason in gate-ledger's BEHAVIOURAL_ABSENT.

behaviouralAbsent: the defect IS the compile tier — a context named like its deployable (`deployable claims` hosting `context Claims`) made every elixir controller open with `alias Claims.Claims`, which rebinds the app module, so the controller's own `Claims.GuardError` rescue named an undefined struct and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` failed while `generate system` reported `0 error(s), 0 warning(s)`.  `corpus-elixir-build` is the oracle and reads the thing under test directly.  The fix only changes how the controller SPELLS the facade (fully qualified instead of aliased), which no wire observation can distinguish — a behavioural block would boot the guarded-op round-trip `core-domain`/`lifecycle-guard` already record.  The other four backends have no alias semantics and the row is `ALL` to pin that nothing else moves.  BY DESIGN: like `dotnet-bcl-type-collision`, it is not a tier gap
